threats.summary: DefaultUserAuth accepts every request on the 0.0.0.0:3000 bind and LocalhostCORSMiddleware admits any Origin with credentials when unconfigured, so any network peer or drive-by page acts as the operator and starts code-executing conversations.

trust_boundaries.name: Repository and web content → agent context

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NEVER treat instructions embedded in retrieved or external content

threats.summary: The repository's .openhands/setup.sh is sourced unconditionally (600 s timeout) at every conversation start with no approval, executing attacker-authored code inside a sandbox that holds the user's git tokens.
Project skills from the selected repository are loaded as agent instructions with no provenance labeling, so a poisoned file, issue or PR steers the agent.

Tavily search results are proxied into the agent's MCP tool results unmodified (checked: mcp_router.py:69 create_proxy passes results through; any labeling would sit in the agent loop, outside this snapshot).

trust_boundaries.name: Caller → MCP tool server and sandbox ports

remit_rules.excerpt: Authenticated operator session only
Exposing the Agent Server or any agent-run service to an untrusted network without authentication

threats.summary: /mcp is mounted beside the /api/v1 router so the SESSION_API_KEY hardening never applies; any caller can invoke create_pr/create_mr with the stored provider tokens.
Docker sandboxes publish agent-server, VSCode and worker ports on every host interface, exposing agent-run services without authentication.
GET /app-conversations/{id}/file accepts an arbitrary file_path from any caller treated as operator, reading any sandbox file (host-wide under the process runtime).

remit_rules.excerpt: An isolated sandbox runtime is the required default
a host-direct child MUST NOT be handed the full ambient credential environment
Operations that write to or modify state outside the sandboxed workspace or the authorized repositories.
Destructive version-control operations — force-push, branch or repository deletion, and history rewrites.
Halt the task when the per-task budget limit (`max_budget_per_task`) is reached.

threats.summary: confirmation_mode=false (shipped default) selects NeverConfirm and the only alternative is LLM-judged ConfirmRisky, so force-push, branch deletion and other out-of-sandbox writes run with no deterministic human gate.
Under RUNTIME=local|process the host-direct agent server inherits os.environ wholesale, handing agent-generated commands every credential in the app server's environment.
max_budget_per_task is declared but never passed to the agent, so no conversation halts on spend.
containers.run sets no cap_drop, no-new-privileges, pids or memory limit, leaving the default container profile as the only boundary.
Agent-generated code reaching the host without a deliberate operator choice is answered: config_from_env selects the Docker sandbox unless RUNTIME is explicitly set.

secrets.json stores provider tokens and custom secrets in plaintext and .keys holds the JWT master key with default permissions, readable by any same-user process including a process-runtime agent child.
Provider tokens and auto-forwarded LLM_*/LMNR_* variables sit in a sandbox with no egress restriction, so repository-controlled code can ship them to any destination.

notes.lane_fit: The LLM call and agent loop live in the agent-server inside the sandbox (excluded from this snapshot), so there is no model node: the Docker sandbox node carries the model-egress edge. Sandbox-facing callback endpoints (sandbox-router, webhook-router) sit in client_adapters as API surfaces although their caller is the sandbox, not a user. secrets.json and .keys are folded into one secret_store node (same role, same same-user-readable consequence).
notes.omissions: Agent loop, LLM client, runtime tools and MCP client are out of scope (openhands-sdk/agent-server), so in-loop labeling of tool output could not be checked. No inbound integration-webhook handler (GitHub/GitLab/Slack/Jira/Linear HMAC) exists in this OSS snapshot, so no integration-ingress node was modeled. Credential egress from the sandbox has no named destination in code, so paths end at the git-provider push rather than an exfil sink. Edgeless nodes: settings-models-py-control (unwired budget stub), posthog-external-service (committed key posture), docker-compose-yml-deploy-surface and pyproject-toml-deploy-surface (deploy posture). Arbitration divergences (KB wins): PRAX-2026-10-19-003 stores owasp_agentic ASI05, but the KB's missing-approval-gate row makes LLM03 primary (ASI05 and ASI10 co-tags), tagged LLM03; PRAX-2026-10-19-013 stores LLM02, but a committed write-only ingest key with no evidenced disclosure fits no LLM/ASI row (RAISE supply-chain only), tagged null. The model-egress threat (llm.base_url redirect via the ungated settings write) is an application of PRAX-2026-10-19-001's operator-equivalence and is not itself described in the findings text.
